digest.component_or_area: store lock ownership and timeout messaging
propositions: A blocked session cannot determine what is holding the store write lock or whether interrupting it is safe, seeing only a bare PID in the LockTimeout error message.

Compaction sweeps are safely interruptible (skipped sweeps are no-ops and the next trigger refolds events), but operators cannot safely act on this guarantee without identifying the holder as a sweep.
The holder identity and interruptibility status are already known to the code at lock acquisition time but never reach the LockTimeout error message.
An operation_label context manager using contextvars can carry an ambient label from sweep entry points through to lock acquisition without modifying compact_txn.py.
The v2 lock stamp format can preserve forward compatibility by encoding the operation label as a colon-free key=value field that older parsers ignore.
The LockTimeout message must include both the operation label (e.g. op=compact-sweep) and a remedy statement explaining that interrupting a compaction sweep is safe and lossless.
